rfi.description: Students and teachers are planning a new day of strikes and demonstrations Tuesday, as talks with the government remain deadlocked, nearly two months after the start of protests by high school and university students.

rfi.title: French PM's move to increase minimum wage fails to convince unions
rfi.description: The French government on Monday announced a 1.6 percent increase in the national minimum wage, alongside a series of measures aimed at easing cost-of-living pressures. However, the decision fell well short of the demands of trade unions, which have called for fresh protests in the coming days.

rfi.title: Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner joins race for French presidency
rfi.description: France's five-time Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner announced on Monday that he would run in next year's presidential election, expressing concern particularly over "the rise of the far right."

rfi.title: 'I still have nightmares': victim of police violence seeks justice six years on
rfi.description: Three French police officers are due to go on trial on Monday over the brutal beating of black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris in 2020 – a case that sparked nationwide outrage over police violence and racism.

rfi.title: Mélenchon bets on radical change as French presidential race takes shape
rfi.description: Leader of the hard-left France Unbowed party Jean-Luc Mélenchon has vowed to pursue an uncompromising programme of radical change, as he bids for the French presidency in 2027 – despite warnings that his divisive politics could ultimately hand victory to far-right National Rally leader Marine Le Pen.

rfi.title: Drop in French food bank collection as rising cost of living hits donations
rfi.description: France’s annual food bank collection has gathered less than expected in the face of the rising cost of living which has left people with less money to spend on donations. The three-day campaign, which ended on Sunday, aimed to collect enough food to provide the equivalent of 20 million meals.

rfi.title: South Africa's ANC records worst-ever result in 'catastrophic' local election
rfi.description: The African National Congress took just 30 percent of the votes in last week's local elections, its worst electoral performance to date, the electoral commission said on Sunday. The party had previously dominated South African politics since the end of apartheid.

rfi.title: G7 talks in Paris weigh impact of US midterms on Trump's foreign policy
rfi.description: G7 foreign ministers are meeting in Paris on Monday, giving the world's top seven industrialised nations their first opportunity to assess how the US midterm elections may affect President Donald Trump's approach to Ukraine, the Middle East and relations with some of Washington's closest allies.

rfi.title: Cop31 opens in Turkey as climate funding and fossil fuels divide nations
rfi.description: United Nations climate talks get under way in Turkey on Monday, as the world heads beyond the 1.5C warming limit and poorer nations seek money to withstand floods and droughts, and countries remain divided over fossil fuels. Delegates from the United States will attend, but will not take part in negotiations.

rfi.title: Turkey courts Egypt to tip the scales in eastern Mediterranean power game
rfi.description: This week’s joint naval exercises between Turkey and Egypt in the eastern Mediterranean are the latest move in a burgeoning partnership, as Ankara intensifies its efforts to draw Cairo closer and loosen its bonds with Turkish rivals Greece, Cyprus and Israel.

rfi.title: French MPs weigh debate on banning conservative TV channel as petition tops 1m
rfi.description: A petition calling for French television channel CNews, often compared to US broadcaster Fox News, to be shut down has received over a million signatures, two days before lawmakers meet to consider whether a ban should be debated in parliament.

rfi.title: Spanish tennis star Alcaraz defeats Shelton to claim Paris Masters title
rfi.description: Second seed Carlos Alcaraz beat third seed Ben Shelton on Sunday to claim the Paris Masters crown for the first time.

rfi.title: Unions vow to keep pressure on French government after fourth wave of protests
rfi.description: Education union chiefs on Sunday vowed to maintain pressure on the government after student organisations called for another day of nationwide strikes and demonstrations on Tuesday.

rfi.title: Ex-army chief Eisenkot given first chance to form government in Israel
rfi.description: Gadi Eisenkot will on Sunday be formally given the chance to put together Israel's next government after elections on 27 October left neither of the main political parties with an overall majority.

rfi.title: Love story: literary speed dating in an age of declining readership
rfi.description: This week saw France hand out its biggest literary awards, the Prix Goncourt and the Prix Renaudot. However, reading is on the decline, with only 56 percent of French people describing themselves as regular readers in 2025, down 5 percentage points from 2023. But might those numbers rise if reading was a way to meet your soulmate?

euronews.title: Vodafone suffers huge net loss on Germany hit but raises full-year outlook
euronews.description: British mobile phone giant Vodafone on Tuesday posted a huge post-tax loss for its first half, linked primarily to a writedown in Germany, but raised its outlook with total revenue increasing.

euronews.title: EU pledges €10 million for Bulgarian Black Sea search, rescue operations
euronews.description: The EU has pledged €10 million for Bulgaria to bolster search and rescue operations in the Black Sea, which is becoming one of the most dangerous transport routes in the world due to continued drone attacks.

euronews.title: Central Asia's first wind farm with large-scale batteries nears completion in Uzbekistan
euronews.description: Twenty-five of the 26 turbines are already supplying the national grid, while the storage system undergoes safety checks. euronews.description: Drone footage shows the aftermath of a massive pile-up involving dozens of vehicles on a foggy highway near Yambol, Bulgaria, where 11 people were killed and dozens injured, according to state media.

euronews.title: Portugal on alert as storm Charles brings red warnings to Madeira
euronews.description: The government warns of flooding, falling trees and power cuts, urging people to shelter "during peaks of rain and wind". Forecasts indicate heavy rain with thunder, six-metre waves and gusts up to 130 km/h, with parts of Madeira under red alert.

euronews.title: Europe must stop 'begging' for seat at Ukraine peace talks, ex-NATO chief warns
euronews.description: Former NATO boss Anders Fogh Rasumussen warned Europe against merely pleading to part of the US-brokered ceasefire talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi, saying that securing a seat at the negotiating table comes through strength, not “begging”.

euronews.title: Stocks rally as investors snap up tech shares at lower prices
euronews.description: Stocks rallied on Tuesday, extending a technology-led surge on Wall Street, as investors took advantage of lower prices following last week's rout. Falling oil prices added to the upbeat mood.

euronews.description: Tokyo says the new equipment will help Manila monitor shipping routes that are also important to Japan.

euronews.description: Dunagan was six years old when he voiced the young deer in the classic Disney animated film. He went on to enlist in the Marine Corps and retired as a Major with three Purple Hearts.

euronews.title: At least 11 dead and dozens injured in Bulgarian motorway pile-up
euronews.description: Drone footage shows cars crushed between lorries in thick fog near Yambol, and the road has been closed in both directions in an incident involving over 50 vehicles.

euronews.description: Around 5,800 people are still living in emergency facilities set up after mass arrivals in the territory at the end of July.

spiegel.description: Rund eine Woche nach dem Tod von Freie-Wähler-Chef Hubert Aiwanger steht sein Nachfolger im Landtag fest: Gastronom Stephan Weckmann aus Straubing erhält ein Mandat. Wer Bayerns Vizeregierungschef wird, bleibt offen.

spiegel.title: USA: Frau soll seit 2024 in einer Wohnung festgehalten worden sein
spiegel.description: Ein Arbeiter hörte ihre Hilferufe: In North Dakota ist eine Frau offenbar über Jahre festgehalten und misshandelt worden. Zwei Verdächtige wurden festgenommen.

spiegel.title: Vincent Kompany: FC Bayern-Trainer nach Hirnhautreizung offenbar zurück
spiegel.description: Bayern-Trainer Vincent Kompany laborierte an einer Hirnhautreizung. Nun scheint es gesundheitlich aber bergauf zu gehen: Laut übereinstimmenden Medienberichten ist er wieder arbeitsbereit.

spiegel.title: BMW lässt wegen fehlender Teile Schichten ausfallen
spiegel.description: BMW muss aktuell wegen fehlender Teile, die von extern kommen, einzelne Schichten in bis zu drei Werken ausfallen lassen. Jede dieser ausgefallenen Schichten dürfte Hunderte Autos betreffen.

spiegel.title: KI: Andrea Nahles rechnet mit Verlust von 800.000 Jobs
spiegel.description: Die Chefin der Bundesarbeitsagentur rechnet damit, dass künstliche Intelligenz in Deutschland viele Arbeitsplätze kostet. Warum sie trotzdem auf eine neue Agentur zur Anwerbung ausländischer Fachkräfte dringt.

spiegel.title: Frankreich droht Iran nach Cyberangriffen mit weiteren Sanktionen
spiegel.description: Paris beschuldigt Teheran, hinter Hackerattacken auf Supermarkt-Kühlanlagen zu stehen. Irans Botschafter musste nun im französischen Außenministerium vorstellig werden – dessen Chef hält sich weitere Schritte offen.

spiegel.title: Maschinenbauer werfen Bundesregierung vor, Reformen zu blockieren
spiegel.description: Fehlende Investitionen, wachsende Bürokratie und unterlassene Reformen, die den Standort Deutschland schwächen. Die Maschinenbauer erheben schwere Vorwürfe gegen die schwarz-rote Koalition.

spiegel.title: Dark Eagle: Hyperschallwaffe oder USA ist immer noch nicht voll einsatzbereit
spiegel.description: Eine neue US-Waffe soll selbst stark verteidigte Ziele treffen. Doch offenbar bremsen Qualitätsprobleme die Produktion. Wie groß ist Chinas Vorsprung – und braucht Deutschland so eine Waffe auch?

spiegel.title: US-Skistar: Lindsey Vonn »ziemlich nervös« vor nächster OP
spiegel.description: Mit einem emotionalen Video gibt Lindsey Vonn Einblicke in ihr Seelenleben. Sie bete dafür, dass die neunte OP der letzte Eingriff sein wird – und rechnet damit, dass sie noch monatelang ausfallen wird.

spiegel.title: Florida: Stimmenrekorder des abgestürzten Privatjets geborgen
spiegel.description: Er könnte ein Puzzlestück bei der Suche nach der Unglücksursache sein: Der Stimmenrekorder des in Florida verunglückten Learjets wurde gefunden. Doch bislang ist unklar, ob er noch funktioniert.

observador.title: Trofa. Detidos seis suspeitos de prática de jogo ilegal
observador.description: Da operação da GNR resultou a elaboração de oito autos de contraordenação, a apreensão de quatro máquinas de jogo e a apreensão de droga. Os detidos têm entre os 20 e os 53 anos.

observador.title: Espectadores em cinemas nacionais aumentam 60,8% em outubro
observador.description: Os cinemas portugueses registaram 10,2 milhões de espectadores nos primeiros 10 meses do ano, mais 1,2 milhões do que no mesmo período de 2025. "Santo António" está no top 5 de filmes mais vistos.

observador.title: UE deve" cortar dependências arriscadas" na tecnologia
observador.description: No palco principal da Web Summit, Henna Virkkunen veio defender que a Europa deve ser mais independente a nível de tecnologia. Mas "a soberania tecnológica não significa isolamento ou proteccionismo".

observador.title: Tilly Norwood, a "atriz" de IA sem botox nem cachet
observador.description: Depois dos robôs, a Web Summit deu palco a Tilly Norwood, uma atriz de Inteligência Artificial. Criadora responde a críticas e diz que é "uma outra forma de contar histórias".

observador.title: Alcione, Zeca Pagodinho e Jorge Aragão no Coala Festival
observador.description: O espetáculo "O Maior Encontro do Samba" juntará em palco os veteranos Zeca Pagodinho, Alcione e Jorge Aragão. Festival realiza-se no Hipódromo Manuel Possolo, em Cascais, no final de maio.

observador.title: José Cid celebra 85 anos no Campo Pequeno em fevereiro
observador.description: O espetáculo "Jovem aos 80" acontece a 4 de fevereiro de 2027. Concerto contará com uma banda de sete músicos, incluindo elementos do Quarteto 1111 e convidados como Marisa Liz e Mário Mata.

observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Peniche. Agricultores pedem centro de recolha de resíduos
observador.description: Presidente da câmara garante estar a ter reuniões para se criar um Centro de Recolha de Resíduos de modo a responder às queixas dos agricultores, que veem na reciclagem da fita uma despesa acrescida

observador.title: Governo espera que IA simplifique processos de construção
observador.description: Governo espera que investimento em IA, para simplificar processos de licenciamento para construção de casas, tenha impacto já no próximo ano. Na Austrália, novas medidas de proteção obrigatórias.

observador.title: Responsáveis de complexo chinês "sob controlo" após fogo
observador.description: Foi anunciada a adoção "medidas de controlo" contra proprietários do imóvel, depois de 14 pessoas morrerem e 25 terem ficado hospitalizadas com incêndio. As causas do fogo estão a ser investigadas.

observador.title: Harry e Meghan em Bruxelas após caso Thomas Markle
observador.description: "A segurança de uma criança nunca deve depender do país onde ela vive", disse o príncipe, no discurso em Bruxelas dias após a detenção do sogro por posse de pornografia infantil.

observador.title: Aguiar-Branco transmite apoio do parlamento a Moçambique
observador.description: Na segunda-feira, os dois parlamentos assinaram um protocolo "que visa criar novas áreas de colaboração, nomeadamente na área do mundo digital e da inteligência artificial".

observador.title: Madeira. Buscas por nadador-salvador retomadas esta terça
observador.description: Nadador-salvador de 37 anos de uma unidade hoteleira do Funchal desapareceu no domingo, depois de alegadamente ter sido arrastado por uma onda. Família já se encontra a receber apoio psicológico.

observador.title: Trump rejeita amnistia e defende política de imigração
observador.description: Presidente dos EUA defendeu política de imigração da Administração, que considera ser "muito forte". E acrescenta que o foco passa por continuar a deportar "os piores dos piores".

observador.title: Rússia abate 155 drones antes de negociações com a Ucrânia
observador.description: O ataque atingiu a rede elétrica da autoproclamada República Popular de Lugansk e causou pelo menos três mortos e quatro feridos. As negociações em Abu Dhabi tiveram início esta terça-feira de manhã.

observador.title: Caldas da Rainha. Nove anos de prisão por 400 crimes sexuais
observador.description: Homem de 46 anos foi intercetado na via pública. Tinha sido condenado pela prática de 400 crimes contra a autodeterminação sexual, 345 na forma agravada, incluindo abuso sexual de crianças.

observador.title: "Impulso positivo" para fim da guerra faz petróleo descer
observador.description: Cotação do crude registava esta terça-feira uma queda de 1,21% no mercado de futuros de Londres, atingindo os 91,45 dólares por barril. Queda prolonga o recuo de mais de 5% na segunda-feira.

observador.title: Interpol detém 262 suspeitas de promoverem tráfico humano

zeit.description: Die SPD wirft der Union vor, ihre Vorschläge zum Bundeshaushalt nicht gegenzufinanzieren. Dabei sei klar: »Was finanziell möglich ist, muss Familien zugutekommen.«

proj-syn.title: Will Anthropic’s IPO Lead to Better AI Regulation?
proj-syn.description: When frontier AI labs go public, ordinary people’s investments and pensions become tied to their valuations and stock prices. While excessive regulation could undermine a firm’s growth, catastrophic accidents caused by inadequate safety measures could do the same—and wipe out shareholder value.

proj-syn.title: A Minimum Basic Income Is Not Enough
proj-syn.description: The rise of AI is concentrating wealth and political power in fewer and fewer hands, making extreme inequality a threat to democracy itself. A universal basic share that gives ordinary people a portion of global profits could help narrow the growing gap between billionaires and everyone else.

proj-syn.title: Scott Bessent’s Risky Short-Termism
proj-syn.description: The US Treasury secretary's commitment to accelerate buybacks of longer-term debt and issue more short-term debt in their place promises significant budgetary savings. But if borrowing costs rise, what happens in the T-bill market won’t stay in the T-bill market.

proj-syn.title: Why Trump Crowned the Man Who Cost Him Congress
proj-syn.description: By appointing Stephen Miller to be his chief of staff, US President Donald Trump has revealed what he cannot give up after decisive midterm losses. The moral depravity of one of the most widely reviled members of his administration is the citadel he will defend until the end.

proj-syn.title: Why Politicians Love Stimulus Checks
proj-syn.description: Stimulus checks sent to households promise to supercharge the economy, but much of the money simply sits in people's bank accounts. They are popular with voters but do little to address the underlying causes of economic downturns and leave future generations to foot the bill.

proj-syn.title: Who’s Winning (and Who’s Losing) the Ocean? — Marie-May Jeremie
proj-syn.description: Ahead of COP31, PS sat down with Marie-May Jeremie, Minister of Environment, Climate, Energy and Natural Resources of the Republic of Seychelles, to discuss the logic of “blue” economic development. Watch as she describes the deeply personal stakes for small island states, and calls on the global community to support their efforts.

proj-syn.title: The Midterms Won’t Change Much for US Allies
proj-syn.description: Even if the Democrats’ midterm victory marks the beginning of the end of the Trump administration’s “America First” approach to foreign affairs, it does not augur the return of a consistent, reliable US foreign policy. America's friends and allies around the world will have to continue to hedge their bets.

proj-syn.title: Revolts of the Young
proj-syn.description: Young protesters have taken to the streets in France, India, Serbia, and several other countries, rising up against corrupt mainstream parties and economic inequality. But their efforts to improve liberal democracy will likely be overshadowed by the far right’s far more organized efforts to seize power.

proj-syn.title: What the ILO Can Teach a Divided World
proj-syn.description: In a world where compromise is held in contempt, collective action is increasingly difficult. The International Labour Organization’s decades-long record of bringing workers, employers, and governments to the negotiating table has been exceptional in this regard, demonstrating the necessity and potential of multilateralism.

proj-syn.title: The Five Stages of AI Grief
proj-syn.description: Like those diagnosed with a terminal illness, humanity is being forced through the stages of denial, anger, bargaining, depression, and acceptance as AI’s capabilities and potential rapidly expand. But there is a crucial difference: AI and its uses are not outside our control.

proj-syn.title: The Economic Toll of Israel’s Wars
proj-syn.description: Israel’s economy may look strong, but three years of war have inflicted far greater damage than its robust stock market and appreciating currency suggest. Defense spending and government borrowing have risen sharply, while falling output and investment point to a prolonged recession.

proj-syn.title: Rebalancing Nature’s Books
proj-syn.description: The first report card on the implementation of the Kunming-Montreal framework was issued at this year’s UN Biodiversity Conference in Yerevan, and the marks were dismal. The problem is not a lack of targets, but a global financial system that pays to destroy nature and penalizes those who protect it.

proj-syn.title: Only Israel’s Arab Parties Can Restore Its Democracy
proj-syn.description: While Israel’s recent election did not deliver the transformation for which many might have hoped, it could open the way to restoring Israeli democracy. By building a coalition with the Arab-led parties, the opposition bloc could defeat not only Benjamin Netanyahu but also the violent, racist ideology he embodies.

proj-syn.title: Making the Most of America’s Midterm Tsunami
proj-syn.description: American voters’ demand for the rule of law and democracy has helped destroy Trump’s MAGA movement. Affordability may have ranked first among their concerns, but addressing it will depend on repairing and improving democratic institutions.

proj-syn.title: AI Can Help Governments Help Citizens
proj-syn.description: In developing economies, the AI debate has focused less on frontier risk and more on how to ensure that the technology actually serves people. That will require not only designing AI tools to work within government, but also investing in the state capacity required to put the technology to use.

proj-syn.title: MAGA’s Midterm Defeat Won’t Change the Course of History
proj-syn.description: The world must not succumb to euphoria following Donald Trump’s latest defeat. If anything, his lame-duck status deprives Americans and everyone else of an excuse for avoiding hard conversations about the truly radical changes that will be needed to avert future catastrophes.

proj-syn.title: Can AI Colonialism Be Prevented?
proj-syn.description: As the United States and China cement their technological dominance, the AI revolution threatens to reproduce the colonial dynamics of the first Industrial Revolution. To avoid digital colonization, middle powers must work together to build an open AI stack and establish common standards to govern it.

proj-syn.title: Turning Sub-Saharan Africa’s Cities Into Job Engines
proj-syn.description: Cities and towns will be central to creating more and better jobs for Sub-Saharan Africa’s fast-growing population, simply because the region’s people and economic activity are increasingly concentrated there. But unlocking urbanization’s potential requires policy guidance and well-planned investment.
